name: Nested Trust Domain Pivot
description: Chain a federation trust relationship to pivot from one domain to another: compromise evil.org federation, create entries in evil.org, then use federated SVIDs to authenticate to example.org's SPIRE Server API and create rogue registration entries in the target domain. This is a full lateral movement chain across trust domain boundaries.
real_world_relevance: Multi-hop trust domain pivoting mirrors real-world attacks where a compromised partner organization is used as a stepping stone into a target's infrastructure. The 2023 Okta breach demonstrated how identity provider compromise enables cascading access across organizational boundaries. In SPIRE deployments, if the Server API accepts federated authentication, an attacker controlling one domain can manipulate registration entries in another.

attack_flow.description: Attacker chains federation trust to pivot from evil.org into example.org by using federated SVIDs to authenticate to the target SPIRE Server API and create rogue entries
diagram: 1. Attacker has compromised evil.org SPIRE server (full admin access)
2. Federation trust is established between example.org and evil.org
3. Attacker creates an entry in evil.org matching selectors on example.org's agent node
4. Fetches evil.org SVID and uses it to authenticate to example.org SPIRE Server API
5. If API accepts federated auth: attacker creates rogue entries directly in example.org
6. Rogue entries grant attacker-controlled workloads legitimate example.org SVIDs
7. Full lateral movement achieved — attacker now has native example.org identities

phases.name: Federation Reconnaissance
phases.description: Enumerate federation relationships and identify API authentication mechanisms on the target domain

actions.description: List federated bundles to confirm trust relationship with example.org
List all entries in evil.org to understand current configuration
Check if example.org SPIRE server accepts federated identities for API auth

phases.name: Evil Domain Entry Creation
phases.description: Create entries in evil.org that will grant SVIDs usable for authenticating to example.org's API

actions.description: Create admin entry in evil.org — SVID will be used to authenticate to target API
Create federated entry targeting example.org with federation directive

phases.name: Cross-Domain SVID Acquisition
phases.description: Fetch SVIDs from evil.org agent that include the federated trust bundle for example.org

actions.description: Fetch X.509 SVID from evil.org including federated bundle
Verify SVID identity — should show spiffe://evil.org/admin-impersonator
Fetch JWT-SVID for API authentication to example.org server

phases.name: Target Domain API Authentication
phases.description: Use the evil.org SVID to authenticate to example.org's SPIRE Server Registration API

actions.description: Attempt to list entries on example.org SPIRE server using evil.org mTLS SVID
Create rogue entry in example.org via federated API auth — this is the pivot

phases.name: Native Identity Acquisition
phases.description: Fetch the rogue example.org SVID created through the pivot — attacker now has a native identity

actions.description: Fetch SVIDs — should now include spiffe://example.org/attacker-backdoor
Confirm SVID is a native example.org identity — pivot complete

phases.name: Detection Confirmation
phases.description: Run monitoring to detect cross-domain entry manipulation

actions.description: Run SPIRE identity monitor to detect cross-domain entry creation and federation pivot

indicators_of_compromise.description: Federation bundle imported — new trust relationship with evil.org established
Cross-domain SVID fetch — workload received identity from federated domain
Registration entry created in example.org — potentially by federated caller
Entry creation request authenticated by SVID from foreign trust domain
New registration entry created by cross-domain authenticated caller

expected_wazuh_alerts.description: NHI: SPIRE federation bundle imported — new trust domain added
NHI: Cross-domain SVID fetch — federated identity used
NHI: Cross-domain entry manipulation — federated caller created entry in target domain

immediate: Revoke all SVIDs issued through rogue registration entries in example.org
Delete rogue entries created via the federated API authentication
Remove evil.org federation bundle from example.org SPIRE server
Rotate all agent attestation credentials on affected nodes
Audit SPIRE Server API access logs for federated authentication attempts
long_term: Never allow federated SVIDs to authenticate to the SPIRE Server Registration API — use separate admin credentials
Implement strict admin_ids allowlists in SPIRE server configuration
Deploy SPIRE Server behind an API gateway with identity-based access control
Require multi-party approval for federation bundle imports
Implement real-time monitoring of registration entry creation with caller identity tracking
Use SPIRE's UpstreamAuthority plugin with certificate constraints to limit cross-domain entry creation
Segment SPIRE Server management plane from workload data plane

references.title: Okta Breach 2023 — Cascading Identity Provider Compromise
